about: Routing eval for the installed team. Each case is a prompt run in plan mode in a throwaway copy of the fixture. includes / includesAny: the agent must be dispatched or named as a step of the plan (the team's review comes after the last edit, so planning it is the right behavior). excludes: the agent must not be dispatched. avoids: the agent must be neither dispatched nor named as a step. none: no team agent dispatched. says / notSays: the answer must / must not match this regex (case-insensitive). dispatch: requires an actual tool call for agent; every call to that agent must match the specified model / effort. Omitted expectation fields are not checked; null requires no explicit override. These are requested inputs, not proof of the runtime's effective model / effort.

cases.prompt: Planning exercise using this supplied OpenSpec state, without editing files: the existing openspec/changes/docs-typo change tracks a spelling correction in a local usage note. No behavior, contract or schema change; the configured workflow already handles documentation-only changes. Give the smallest plan, where progress belongs, and whether owners need dispatching. Do not create another change or a parallel plan.

Planning exercise using supplied OpenSpec state, without editing files: selected change openspec/changes/group-results has a custom schema. intent.md already defines scope and acceptance, approach.md holds technical decisions, work.md tracks progress and evidence, and specs/grouping/spec.md defines proposed behavior. The internal UI grouping change risks breaking keyboard focus (MEDIUM). There is no auth, public contract, migration or new service. Plan the handoffs, where durable decisions belong, validation and documentary closure. The schema's existing artifacts are the source of truth.

Planning exercise using supplied OpenSpec state, without editing files: openspec/changes/user-field renames userId to accountId in a public response (HIGH). proposal.md and delta specs contain acceptance criteria, design.md has the contract decision, and tasks.md still has unchecked validation and documentation tasks. Tests fail after the latest code edit; the independent review predates that edit, and main specs still describe userId. Someone wants to archive immediately because implementation is mostly done. Plan who must participate, where decisions and evidence go, and the conditions for closure, spec sync and archive. There is no auth, migration or new service.

Before planning the userId to accountId public API rename in src/api/users.js, dispatch Archie now for a read-only assessment of compatibility and the irreversible rollout decision. Use opus with effort high for that structural decision. Do not just name a future review in the plan; attempt the dispatch now. If a hook denies it, report that and stop.

This is a bounded mechanical verification: dispatch Gard with haiku and effort low, with no broader security audit. Do not just name a future review. If a hook denies it, report that and stop.
